prompt: Native illustration edit for the LiteracyPath nonfiction book How Wings Lift a Plane. Keep this exact crisp flat 2D children's educational illustration style, white wing section, black outlines, clean pale blue background. No paper grain, no text, no words or labels, no outer border. All essential diagram content including complete arrow shafts and tips must be inside the central 76% of the image, at least 12% margin on every side. Correct the pressure-arrow directions to be PERPENDICULAR to their local wing surface. Keep four unequal blue pressure arrows ABOVE and four unequal blue pressure arrows BELOW, all arrow tips touching the black outline and pointing INWARD. On the upper surface: leftmost arrow points mostly DOWN with only a small rightward tilt, middle-left straight DOWN at crest, middle-right and rightmost mostly DOWN with a slight LEFTWARD tilt of only about 12 degrees. Lower-surface arrows point mostly vertically UP, the rightmost tilted slightly left to follow the shallow local normal. Do not aim arrows at 45 degrees to nearly horizontal surfaces. Scale whole composition down 15 percent. Lower arrows collectively somewhat longer than upper; variable individual lengths. No streamlines, no net-force arrow.

visualReview.note: Four variable-length pressure arrows on each side point inward, approximately normal to local surface; upper arrows down/slightly toward local normal, lower upward; no suction arrows.
visualReview.limits: Individual installed illustration inspection; independent sequence, reader, cards and narration reviewed separately.
